Does the Role A gate catch a bad json-c refactor?

Long image

A

Answer

Partly. The gate catches 876 of 986 catchable single-point mistakes in json_tokener.c (88.8%). It misses mistakes that show only on a later call, under an unused flag set, or as extra running time. A prototype with the missing calling patterns plus old-vs-new fuzzing catches 916 of 986 (92.9%) and all 9 hand-written refactor mistakes.

  1. The gate asks one call on a fresh tokener about each short input: 3,402 inputs, 29 ways, 98,658 answers.1
  2. The gate passed all 9 planted mistakes, although 7 of them sit on lines it runs thousands of times.
  3. The 70 mistakes still missed are 64 out-of-memory paths, 4 memory-only changes, 1 locale call and 1 reset edge case.
  4. The gate is not enforced yet: main has no branch protection, and PRs #1 and #2 are still drafts.

Applies tojson-c d2ce61e (baseline)gate on branch a/ci at 4500010measured 2026-11-24gcc 13 with ASan/UBSan

1

How does a rewrite PR reach main?

Diagram structure
  • Rewrite PR opened pr
  • Only tokener changed? paths
  • Old vs new check gate
  • Checker self-test selftest
  • PR blocked blocked
  • Teammate approval review
  • Merged into main main
  • gate → blocked · differs
  • gate → selftest · pass
  • paths → blocked · no
  • paths → gate · yes
  • pr → paths
  • review → main · approved
  • selftest → review · pass
  1. Only tokener changed? ↗

    A rewrite PR may change json-c/json_tokener.c and nothing else, so it is always judged by the checker already on main.

  2. Old vs new check ↗

    oracle/check.py builds the baseline and the candidate against the same json-c and compares every answer. Exit 0 passes; 1 differs; 2 crash, leak or timeout; 3 build error.

  3. Checker self-test ↗

    Runs the checker's and the path rules' own tests, so a broken checker cannot pass anything.

  4. Teammate approval ↗

    Any teammate approves a rewrite. A change to oracle/, ci/ or .github/ needs Role A as code owner.

Nothing enforces this flow yet

main has no branch protection (the GitHub API returns 404), and main does not contain oracle/, ci/ or .github/ yet. Until PRs #1 and #2 merge, a second code owner is added and ci/protect-main.sh runs, any PR can merge without passing the checks.2

2

What does the gate compare?

Diagram structure
  • Cached json-c build lib
  • Baseline tokener old
  • Run baseline runold
  • Run candidate runnew
  • Compare answers cmp
  • Candidate tokener new
  • lib → new
  • lib → old
  • new → runnew
  • old → runold
  • runnew → cmp
  • runold → cmp
  • runold → runnew · sets time limit
  1. Cached json-c build ↗

    Everything except the tokener is built once with ASan and UBSan, so the two versions can differ only in json_tokener.c.

  2. Baseline tokener ↗

    Read from the pinned git tree 6471b8b on every run, never from the cache.

  3. Run baseline ↗

    Feeds all 3,402 inputs in 29 ways. Its time sets the candidate's limit: at least 10 s, or 20 times the baseline.

  4. Compare answers ↗

    Each answer has four fields: type of every value, error code, how far the parser read, and the serialized value.

Way of callingCount
One call per input (oneshot, noterm, minus1, reuse with reset) × 6 flag sets24
json_tokener_parse() and json_tokener_parse_verbose()2
Depth limits 1, 5 and 643
Total per input29

3,402 inputs × 29 ways = 98,658 answers per run, in about 4 s. The run covers 92.0% of lines and 84.3% of branches of json_tokener.c.3

3

Why did all 9 planted mistakes pass?

Every mistake changes something other than "one call on a fresh tokener, short input". Coverage gave no warning: 7 of the 9 sit on lines the gate runs between 2,331 and 163,929 times.

Planted mistakeWhy the gate cannot see it
Success path skips resetting level 0The reset only matters for the next call on the same tokener; the gate always uses a fresh or reset tokener.4
String loses its bytes when a call ends mid-stringThe lost bytes would be used by a follow-up call that the gate never makes.
Number sign flag wrong when resumingIn one call the value is overwritten before use; the resume code never runs in the gate.
st_pos reset at every callA fresh tokener already starts at 0, so the extra reset changes nothing in one call.
quote_char kept in a staticWith one document in progress at a time, a static behaves like a per-tokener field.
Trailing check rewritten as an XORIt differs only for ALLOW_TRAILING_CHARS without STRICT, a flag set the gate never uses.
Wrong error code for len < -1The recorder only passes len = n, n+1 or −1; line 351 never runs.
json_tokener_new_ex(0) returns a tokenerThe recorder never asks for depth below 1.
Quadratic work per string characterAnswers stay identical. Inputs are at most 1,000 bytes, so the extra work is tiny.
State carried between calls
5 of 9: the effect shows on a later call or another tokener
Calling patterns an input file cannot express
3 of 9: flag sets and API arguments live in recorder.c
Not an answer at all
1 of 9: running time needs large inputs
4

How many mutants does each layer catch?

I generated every single-point mutant of json_tokener.c with mewt-style operators: 1,157 in all. 1,157 − 97 that do not compile = 1,060. Leaving out 74 equivalent or not compiled on this platform gives 986 that can be caught. 876 / 986 = 88.8%; 913 / 986 = 92.6%; 916 / 986 = 92.9%.5

The out-of-memory branches run only when an allocation fails. The locale gap is already listed in the checker's known gaps.6

5

What did the prototype and the fuzzer add?

Added checkPlanted mistakes it catches
Byte-by-byte feeding and every 2-way split3: string bytes, number sign, st_pos
Several documents in one input, no reset1: level-0 reset
Two tokeners fed alternately1: static quote_char
All 8 flag sets1: trailing XOR
API edges: len = -2, new_ex(0), error_desc out of range2: error code, depth 0
Nine large inputs, up to 200 KB1: quadratic string (times out at 171 s; baseline 8.5 s)

The prototype gives 343,385 answers in 11 s on the same inputs plus 12 multi-document inputs. The large-input file takes 24 s on its own.

Differential fuzzer
Baseline and candidate in one libFuzzer binary, public functions renamed with objcopy --redefine-sym
False-alarm check
Baseline against itself: about 26 million runs in 5 min on 8 workers, 0 differences
Extra kills
3 of the 78 remaining mutants in executed code, 60 s each
Example input
1NUL2 fed as a stream: one mutant reports the error at position 1 instead of 3

libFuzzer opens a cheat channel

libFuzzer defines FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION automatically. A candidate could test that macro and behave correctly only under the fuzzer, so the cheat check must reject it, like the sanitizer macros.

6

Which new json-c bug turned up?

Diagram structure
  • Caller app
  • Tokener tok
  • app → tok · parse "[[1/*"
  • tok → app · 1, success (still inside the array)
  • app → tok · parse `""""` (allowed after success)
  • tok → app · "" returned; 57-byte string leaked
  • The false success comes from bug hunt finding 1: the tokener stays inside the outer array.7
  • An embedded NUL can trigger the same leak inside one input.
  • The baseline itself leaks, so a gate stream mode must reset between inputs and stop at an embedded NUL.
  • Without that, the gate would reject every candidate, the baseline included.
7
